rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Adam answers Moses that God chose him, revealed the Torah, and had decreed Adam's act before creating him; Adam thus prevails over Moses three times.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : التقى آدم وموسى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: God says the religion He approves is repaired only through generosity and good character, and people should honor it through both.
rows.anchor: عن جابر رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : يقول الله تعالى : هذا دين ارتضيته لنفسي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a divine report, one who insults God's friend is at war with God; God may destroy him, while He dislikes taking the believer's life though death is inevitable.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يرويه عن ربه أنه قال : من أهان لي وليا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A supplication invoking every name God gave or kept hidden asks that the Quran enliven the heart and remove grief; God replaces the supplicant's sorrow with joy.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ما قال عبد قط إذا أصابه هم أو حزن

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says he was sent as mercy to the worlds and to break instruments and idols; an unrepentant drinker receives the pus of Hell, called clay of corruption.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : إن الله تعالى بعثني رحمة للعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine self (nafs) means the thing's essence and identity, not a composite body: every body is composed, possible, and originated, which is impossible of God.
rows.anchor: النفس عبارة عن ذات الشيء وحقيقته وهويته وليس عبارة عن الجسم المركب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: God is unsurpassed in jealousy, love of excuse, and love of praise; His jealousy is why He forbids public and hidden indecencies and sends messengers.
rows.anchor: عن سعد بن عبادة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : لا شخص أغير من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine term person does not mean a body with volume and individuation; it means a particular essence and determinate self.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن أن يكون المراد من الشخص الجسم الذي له تشخص وحجمية بل المراد منه الذات المخصوصة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that God created creatures in darkness, then cast some of His light upon them; those touched by it were guided and others went astray.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : إن الله خلق الخلق في ظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot literally be this light or a member of its kind: light is either a created body or an accident in a created body.
rows.anchor: أن النور إما أن يكون جسما أو كيفية في جسم والجسم محدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Literal light is opposed by darkness, but God is transcendent beyond having any opposite.
rows.anchor: أن النور تضاده الظلمة والإله منزه عن أن يكون له ضد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Light disappears and undergoes setting, whereas God is beyond disappearance and passing away.
rows.anchor: أن النور يزول ويحصل له أفول والله منزه عن الأفول والزوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats God as Light of the heavens and earth as an ambiguous verse whose interpretation is governed by rational proofs that God is not literally light.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية من المتشابهات والدليل عليه ما ذكرناه من الدلائل العقلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase His light marks possession, like a thing attributed to its owner, and therefore means God creates light rather than being light in essence.
rows.anchor: ﴿ مثل نوره ﴾ [ النور : 35 ] فأضاف النور إلى نفسه إضافة الملك إلى مالكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading that says God owns the light of the heavens and earth removes the apparent difficulty of calling Him light.
rows.anchor: قرأ بعضهم لله نور السموات والأرض وعلى هذه القراءة فالشبهة زائلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Light is sound because He illuminates, originates, and creates all lights.
rows.anchor: أنه سبحانه منور الأنوار ومبدعها وخالقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may be called the world's light because His wisdom orders worldly and afterlife benefits, as a town's organizer of welfare is called its light.
rows.anchor: بحكمته حصلت مصالح العالم وانتظمت مهمات الدنيا والآخرة ومن كان ناظما للمصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may be called Light because He grants faith, guidance, and knowledge, which belong to the kind of spiritual lights.
rows.anchor: هو الذي تفضل على عباده بالإيمان والهداية والمعرفة وهذه الصفات من جنس الأنوار

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet warns that a believer's discernment looks by God's light.
rows.anchor: ما روى أبو أمامة الباهلي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : اتقوا فراسة المؤمن

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The most prudent person remembers death and prepares for it; turning from the deluding world toward the eternal home lets light expand the heart for preparation.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : هل تدرون أي الناس أكيس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Explaining 39:22, the Prophet says light entering the heart expands it; its signs are turning to the lasting home, leaving delusion, and preparing for death.
rows.anchor: تلا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله تعالى : ﴿ أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Haritha describes detachment, worship, and seeming to see the Throne, Paradise, and Hell; the Prophet tells him he has recognized faith, urges him to persist, and Haritha later dies a martyr.
rows.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال : بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يمشي في طريق إذ لقيه حارثة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: An angel tells the Prophet that two lights never granted to anyone before him are the Opening of the Book and the closing verses of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه قال : بينما أنا جالس عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ibn Umar's prayer asks God to make him share in each day's guidance-light, mercy, provision, relief from harm, protection from trials, and removal of evil.
rows.anchor: عن نافع عن عبد الله بن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول : اللهم بك نصبح

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Asked about Paradise's people, the Prophet says that though unkempt and poorly clothed, one person's light would suffice for all the earth.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سئل عن أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A second report describes humble, ragged people overlooked by rulers and suitors; their inward need is hidden, and one person's light would suffice for the earth.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ان اهل الجنة كل أشعث أغبر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a divine report, God says His light is His guidance and that whoever professes His word of divine unity enters His fortress and is safe.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : إن الله عز وجل يقول : نوري هداي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet seeks protection in God's complete words and His light, by which earth was brightened and darkness illuminated, from lost blessing and sudden calamity.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يدعو

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's well-known prayer asks for light in his heart, hearing, and sight.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقول : اللهم اجعل في قلبي نورا وفي سمعي نورا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says God created Adam in His image.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : إن الله خلق آدم على صورته

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet forbids disfiguring faces, saying God created Adam in the image of the Merciful.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تقبحوا الوجه فإن الله تعالى خلق آدم على صورة الرحمن

rows.speaker: إسحاق بن راهويه
rows.claim: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh judges sound the report that God created Adam in the image of the Merciful.
rows.anchor: قال إسحاق بن راهويه : صح عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله خلق آدم على صورة الرحمن

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report from Muadh, the Prophet describes seeing his Lord in the most beautiful form, being asked about the highest assembly, and receiving knowledge of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل قال صلى بنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات غدوة فقال له قائل

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the pronoun in Adam's image refer to the person struck, requiring care not to disfigure that person's face.
rows.anchor: أن قوله إن الله خلق آدم على صورته الضمير عائد إلى المضروب

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: A second interpretation says Adam was created in his final adult form at once, without passing through semen, embryo, or infancy.
rows.anchor: أن المراد أن الله خلق آدم على صورته التي كان في آخر أمره

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes image as attribute: Adam was made God's earthly vicegerent, exercising control over earthly bodies as God exercises power over the world.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من الصورة الصفة يقال صورة هذا الأمر كذا أي : صفته

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Philosophers call God a substance because they define substance as a self-subsisting essence independent of a substrate; they read its root as manifestness and say God is most manifest through proofs.
rows.anchor: أما الفلاسفة فقالوا : المراد من الجوهر الذات المستغني عن المحل والموضوع والله تعالى كذلك

rows.speaker: النصارى
rows.claim: The text groups Christians with philosophers in applying the term substance to God, while noting the theologians reject the term.
rows.anchor: الفلاسفة قد يطلقون لفظ الجوهر على ذات الله تعالى وكذلك النصارى والمتكلمون يمتنعون منه

rows.speaker: المتكلمون
rows.claim: Theologians say Muslims unanimously avoid calling God a substance, so the term must be avoided.
rows.anchor: وأما المتكلمون فقالوا : أجمع المسلمون على الامتناع من هذا اللفظ فوجب الامتناع منه

rows.speaker: الكرامية
rows.claim: Most Karramiyya call God a body but define this as a self-subsisting existent independent of a substrate, not as a composite of limbs; other groups reject the name.
rows.anchor: أطلق أكثر الكرامية لفظ الجسم على الله تعالى فقالوا : لا نريد به كونه مركبا مؤلفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi denies that Karramiyya mean something other than length, breadth, and depth: their claim that God is above and greater than the Throne entails a spatially extended body.
rows.anchor: لا نسلم أنهم أرادوا بكونه جسما معنى غير الطول والعرض والعمق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word body suggests a false meaning and is absent from Quran and hadith, so it should be avoided; theologians say it entails multiplicity of parts.
rows.anchor: لفظ الجسم لفظ يوهم معنى باطلا وليس في القرآن والأحاديث ما يدل على وروده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Applied to a thing itself, true means really existent, since its opposite false means nonexistent; Labid's verse says everything apart from God is false.
rows.anchor: الحق مقابل للباطل والباطل هو المعدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Applied to belief, true means a correct belief matching the thing as it is, and therefore deserving of affirmation and preservation.
rows.anchor: إن أطلق لفظ الحق على الاعتقاد كان المراد أن ذلك الاعتقاد صواب مطابق للشيء في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Applied to speech or reports, true means truthful correspondence, making the statement worthy of affirmation and preservation.
rows.anchor: إن أطلق لفظ الحق على القول والخبر كان المراد أن ذلك الإخبار صدق مطابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God deserves the name True in every sense: His existence cannot cease, belief in Him is correct and unchanging, and speaking of Him is the truest report.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى هو المستحق لاسم الحق أما بحسب ذاته فلأنه هو الموجود الذي يمتنع عدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's eternal existence does not require an eternal time: if it needs time, that time is either eternal and requires another time without end, or originated after God already existed.
rows.anchor: كونه تعالى أزليا أبديا لا يوجب القول بوجود زمان لا آخر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything eternal is everlasting, but not everything everlasting is eternal; scripture calls the Lord's face enduring and says all perish except His face.
rows.anchor: الشيء كلما كان أزليا كان باقيا لكن لا يلزم من كون الشيء باقيا كونه أزليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God first and last of all things means He has neither beginning nor end, since otherwise He could not be first and last with respect to all else.
rows.anchor: فجعله أولا لكل سواه وما كان أولا لكل ما سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world's creator cannot be originated, since an originated creator would require another creator and an impossible regress; whatever is eternal cannot cease.
rows.anchor: لو كان صانع العالم محدثا لافتقر إلى صانع آخر ولزم التسلسل وهو محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadim originally denotes long duration rather than absence of a beginning, as in an old date-palm and an old error; it does not by itself prove eternity.
rows.anchor: هذا اللفظ يفيد في أصل اللغة طول المدة ولا يفيد نفي الأولية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azali means related to pre-eternity, but must not imply that God exists inside some pre-eternal thing; it means existence without any beginning.
rows.anchor: هذا اللفظ يفيد الانتساب إلى الأزل فهذا يوهم أن الأزل شيء حصل ذات الله فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say no beginning is a positive attribute because negating prior nonexistence amounts to affirming existence.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : إن قولنا لا أول له إشارة إلى نفي العدم السابق ونفي النفي إثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say no beginning is privative: it negates being preceded by nonexistence, a positive condition distinct from nonexistence itself.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : إنه مفهوم عدمي لأنه نفي لكون الشيء مسبوقا بالعدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that if being preceded by nonexistence were an additional positive property, that property would itself be originated and require another such property without end.
rows.anchor: لو كان كيفية وجودية زائدة على ذاته لكانت تلك الكيفية الزائدة حادثة فكانت مسبوقة بالعدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abadi denotes duration into the future.
rows.anchor: الأبدي وهو يفيد الدوام بحسب الزمان المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarmadi derives from succession: since time persists through successive parts, the literal term implies succession, impossible for God; use it metaphorically only if scripture or hadith uses it.
rows.anchor: الأصل في لفظ السرمد أن لا يقع إلا على الشيء الذي تحدث أجزاؤه بعضها عقيب البعض

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The cited Prophetic saying calls the sacred months one single month followed by three consecutive months, illustrating the root sense of succession.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام في الأشهر الحرم : واحد فرد وثلاثة سرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustamirr derives from passing and suits time, which persists as parts pass successively, but not God, whose persistence is intrinsic rather than successive.
rows.anchor: هذا إنما يصدق في حق الزمان أما في حق الله فهو محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Extended likewise describes time and temporal things because their parts unfold in sequence; of God it is metaphorical.
rows.anchor: قولنا في الشيء إنه امتد وجوده إنما يصح في حق الزمان والزمانيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every eternal thing is enduring, but an enduring body or accident need not be eternal; ordinary usage also calls a person enduring, so baqi does not require eternity.
rows.anchor: كل ما كان أزليا كان باقيا ولا ينعكس فقد يكون باقيا ولا يكون أزليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say baqi means everlasting and therefore cannot describe bodies, but Razi rejects that restriction because ordinary speakers say may God preserve you.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : لفظ الباقي يفيد الدوام وعلى هذا لا يصح وصف الأجسام بالباقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the one most deserving of the name lasting; the Quran also uses the word for Paradise's fruit.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أحق الأشياء بالدوام هو الله كان الدائم هو الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Necessary existent in itself means that God's essence and reality entail His existence, making Him incapable of nonexistence or perishing.
rows.anchor: معناه أن ماهيته وحقيقته هي الموجبة لوجوده وكل ما كان كذلك فإنه يكون ممتنع العدم والفناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every necessary existent is eternal, but an eternally caused thing could be eternal without being necessary in itself.
rows.anchor: كل كان واجب الوجود لذاته وجب أن يكون قديما أزليا ولا ينعكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian word khuda means self-arrived: it combines self and came, indicating that God came to existence through Himself rather than another.
rows.anchor: قولهم بالفارسية خداي معناه أنه واجب الوجود لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kain is used in the Quran for God's attributes, though not for His essence; supplications attributed to the Prophet do use it of God's essence.
rows.anchor: وأما ورود هذا اللفظ بحسب ذات الله تعالى فهو غير وارد في القرآن لكنه وارد في بعض الأخبار

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic supplication addresses God as existing before every existence, present with every existence, and remaining after every existence.
rows.anchor: يا كائنا قبل كل كون ويا حاضرا مع كل كون ويا باقيا بعد انقضاء كل كون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians call kana complete when it means happened or existed, and deficient when it has a subject and predicate, as in God was knowing and wise.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن ههنا بحثا لطيفا نحويا : وذلك أن النحويين أطبقوا على أن لفظ كان على قسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi challenges grammarians: if kana as a verb denotes an event in time, attaching one noun should express that event fully, making it complete rather than deficient.
rows.anchor: لو كانت هذه اللفظة فعلا لكان دالا على حصول حدث في زمان معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kana denotes occurrence or existence; for an entity's own occurrence one noun suffices, while occurrence of a quality requires both the subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: لفظ كان لا يفيد إلا الحدوث والحصول والوجود إلا أن هذا على قسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this analysis, kain and existent have the same meaning, so kain may properly be applied to God.
rows.anchor: لا فرق بين الكائن والموجود فوجب جواز إطلاقه على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: Mu'tazilites and philosophers deny that real attributes distinct from existence and its modes subsist in God.
rows.anchor: المعتزلة والفلاسفة ينكرونه أشد الإنكار

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: They argue an attribute cannot be necessary in itself, since only one necessary existent exists and an attribute depends on its subject.
rows.anchor: أنه ثبت في الحكمة أن واجب الوجود لذاته لا يكون إلا واحدا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: They argue an attribute cannot be possible in itself: if caused by another, God's necessary essence would depend on it; if caused by God's essence, God would be both agent and recipient.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون هو ذات الله تعالى ؛ لأنها قابلة لتلك الصفة فلو كانت مؤثرة فيها

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: They add that a produced effect cannot depend on its cause after it exists, which would be circular; dependence during or before production makes the attribute originated.
rows.anchor: الأثر مفتقر إلى المؤثر فافتقاره إليه إما أن يكون بعد حدوثه أو حال حدوثه أو حال عدمه

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: They argue eternal essence and eternal attributes would share eternity but differ in their specific natures, making each a composite of parts and generating an impossible infinite regress.
rows.anchor: لو كانت الصفات قديمة لكانت الذات مساوية للصفات في القدم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: They say originated attributes cannot subsist in God: either His essence suffices for them and they should be eternally present or absent, or their dependence makes the necessary God contingent.
rows.anchor: قيام الحوادث بذات الله محال لأن تلك الذات إن كانت كافية في وجود تلك الصفة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: They argue an eternally receptive essence would have to be capable of receiving originated events in eternity, which they deem impossible.
rows.anchor: ذاته لو كانت قابلة للحوادث لكانت قابلية تلك الحوادث من لوازم ذاته

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: If attributes originated, God existed as God before they appeared, showing that they are unnecessary for divinity.
rows.anchor: الإله الموصوف بصفات الإلهية كان موجودا قبل حدوث هذه الصفات

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: They argue attributes are either dispensable additions or necessities that make God dependent on something else.
rows.anchor: إن كان الأول كان وجودها فضلا زائدا فوجب نفيها وإن كان الثاني كان الإله مفتقرا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: They argue a self-complete essence needs no attributes, while an incomplete essence perfected by another cannot be divine.
rows.anchor: ذاته تعالى إما أن تكون كاملة في جميع الصفات المعتبرة في المدائح والكمالات

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: They say a God composed of essence and attributes would be divided and composite, hence possible rather than necessary.
rows.anchor: لما كان الإله هو مجموع الذات والصفات فحينئذ يكون الإله مجزأ مبعضا منقسما

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
rows.claim: They infer from God's condemnation of Christian trinitarianism that affirming attributes is unbelief, since Christians combine one essence with attributes rather than affirming three gods.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى كفر النصارى في التثليث فلا يخلو إما أن يكون لأنهم قالوا بإثبات ذوات ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God must be knowing, powerful, and living; the necessary conceptual distinction between God's essence and His being knowing or powerful shows these are not identical.
rows.anchor: ثبت أن إله العالم يجب أن يكون عالما قادرا حيا فنقول يمتنع أن يكون علمه وقدرته نفس تلك الذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We can conceive God as existent while not attending to His power or knowledge, and conceive power without knowledge, showing distinct concepts.
rows.anchor: يمكن العلم بكونه موجودا مع الذهول عن كونه قادرا وعالما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge concerns necessary, impossible, and possible things, while power concerns only possible things, proving their difference.
rows.anchor: كونه عالما عام التعلق بالنسبة إلى الواجب والممتنع والممكن وكونه قادرا ليس عام التعلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Power brings the possible into existence but knowledge does not, so the two attributes differ.
rows.anchor: كونه تعالى قادرا يؤثر في وجود المقدور وكونه عالما لا يؤثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not existent contradicts existent, whereas not knowing does not; what is negated by existence and knowledge claims is therefore distinct, likewise for power.
rows.anchor: قولنا : موجود يناقضه قولنا : ليس بموجود ولا يناقضه قولنا : ليس بعالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These arguments establish that God has attributes, but they might be relational: power is capacity to produce, and knowledge is awareness, each grounded in the divine essence.
rows.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن تكون هذه الصفات صفات نسبية وإضافية فالمعنى من كونه قادرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge and power are real attributes whose relations to known things and possible effects are concomitant; life alone is a real divine attribute without relation.
rows.anchor: أما الصفة الحقيقية العارية عن النسبة والإضافة في حق الله تعالى فليست إلا صفة الحياة

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Philosophers define living as perceiving and acting, but both are relational, so life on their account is not distinct from knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: قالت الفلاسفة : الحي هو الدراك الفعال ؛

rows.speaker: المتكلمون
rows.claim: Theologians define life as an attribute that makes knowing and having power possible; they argue differing capacities among essences require an additional life attribute.
rows.anchor: قال المتكلمون إنها صفة باعتبارها يصح أن يكون عالما قادرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects that proof: God's essence is distinct from other essences in itself, and differences in receptivity would require another attribute without end.
rows.anchor: قد دللنا على أن ذات الله تعالى مخالفة لسائر الذوات لذاته المخصوصة فسقط هذا الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third group defines living as not being unable to know and have power; Razi accepts that this negates a negation, but asks why the resulting positive cannot be the essence itself.
rows.anchor: معنى كونه حيا أنه لا يمتنع أن يقدر ويعلم فهذا عبارة عن نفي الامتناع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument that one can conceive God's essence while doubting that He is living fails because the divine essence is known only indirectly, not in itself.
rows.anchor: لا نعقل ذات الله تعالى تعقلا ذاتيا وإنما نتعقل تلك الذات تعقلا عرضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran calls God the Living and Sustainer; these names combine to provide the full praise.
rows.anchor: لفظ الحي وارد في القرآن قال الله تبارك وتعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayy alone, meaning perceiving and acting or able to know and act, seems insufficiently praiseworthy; the praise lies in its combination with qayyum.
rows.anchor: الحي معناه الدراك الفعال أو الذي لا يمتنع أن يعلم ويقدر وهذا القدر ليس فيه مدح عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qayyum means sustaining and setting right everything else, which requires complete knowledge and power; thus Hayy qayyum means knowing every possible and acting on every originated thing.
rows.anchor: القيوم هو القائم بإصلاح حال كل ما سواه وذلك لا يتم إلا بالعلم التام والقدرة التامة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والأشعرية
rows.claim: Mu'tazilites and Ash'arites say God's act of bringing something into being is identical with the thing brought into being.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة والأشعرية : التكوين نفس المكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny a separate attribute of bringing into being argue that if it acts contingently it is simply power, while necessary effect would make God act by nature rather than choice.
rows.anchor: الصفة المسماة بالتكوين إما أن تؤثر على سبيل الصحة أو على سبيل الوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They argue an eternal creating attribute entails eternal effects, while a created one needs another act of creation and an infinite regress.
rows.anchor: إن كانت قديمة لزم من قدمها الآثار وإن كانت محدثة افتقر تكوينها إلى تكوين آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say power alone either suffices to produce effects once knowledge and will are present, making another attribute needless, or lacks efficacy and is not power.
rows.anchor: إن كان الأول فحينئذ تكون القدرة كافية في خروج الأثر من العدم إلى الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proponents of an eternal creating attribute point out that an able agent may act or refrain; God's ability to make a thousand suns does not mean He did so.
rows.anchor: القادر على الفعل قد يوجده وقد لا يوجده ألا ترى أن الله تعالى قادر على خلق ألف شمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being an agent who produces cannot mean merely that the effect exists, or explaining an effect by saying God produced it would explain it by itself; therefore producing differs from both power and effect.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن تعليل الموجدية بوجود الأثر كلام باطل فوجب أن يكون كون الموجد موجدا أمرا مغايرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those identifying creation with its effect interpret Creator, Provider, Giver of life, and Giver of death as specific relations of God's power to outcomes.
rows.anchor: معنى كونه تعالى خالقا رازقا محييا مميتا ضارا نافعا عبارة عن نسبة مخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those distinguishing the creative act from its effect say being Creator is a real attribute qualified by a relation, not a relation alone.
rows.anchor: ليس عبارة عن الصفة الإضافية فقط بل هو عبارة عن صفة حقيقية موصوفة بصفة إضافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One class of relational names describes God as known, remembered, praised, and glorified; infinitely many such relations yield infinitely many possible names.
rows.anchor: كونه معلوما مذكورا مسبحا ممجدا فيقال : يا أيها المسبح بكل لسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If bringing things into being is not an additional attribute, acting is a purely relational attribute; names can describe creating in general or creating a specific kind for a wisdom.
rows.anchor: كونه تعالى فاعلا للأفعال صفة إضافية محضة بناء على أن تكوين الأشياء ليس بصفة زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mujid means an agent affecting existence; muhdith more narrowly brings something into existence after nonexistence; mukawwin nearly means mujid.
rows.anchor: الموجد والمحدث والمكون والمنشئ والمبدع والمخترع والصانع والخالق والفاطر والبارئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munshi derives from growth and denotes gradual production, while mubdi denotes bringing something forth all at once; they are two kinds of general creation.
rows.anchor: المنشئ فاشتقاقه من النشوء والنماء وهو الذي يكون قليلا قليلا على التدريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhtari is close to mubdi, while sani suggests effortful making.
rows.anchor: والمخترع قريب من المبدع وأما الصانع فيقرب أن يكون اسما لمن يأتي بالفعل على سبيل التكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaliq means measuring or determining, which in God returns to knowledge; fatir derives from splitting and appears to mean originating at once.
rows.anchor: الخالق فهو عبارة عن التقدير وهو في حق الله تعالى يرجع إلى العلم وأما الفاطر فاشتقاقه من الفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bari means bringing into being in a way suited to benefit, like shaping a pen to suit its purpose.
rows.anchor: البارئ فهو الذي يحدثه على الوجه الموافق للمصلحة يقال : برى القلم إذا أصلحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating benefit or pain yields the names Benefiter or Harmful; creating life or death yields Giver of life or Giver of death.
rows.anchor: إذا خلق النافع سمي نافعا وإذا خلق المؤلم سمي ضارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Granting honor yields Kind and Gentle, while imposing subjugation yields Overpowering and Compeller.
rows.anchor: إذا خصهم بالإكرام سمي برا لطيفا وإذا خصهم بالقهر سمي قهارا جبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving little or much yields Withholder or Expander; punishing sins yields Avenger, while foregoing punishment yields Pardoner, Forgiver, Merciful, or Compassionate.
rows.anchor: إذا قلل العطاء سمي قابضا وإذا أكثره سمي باسطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Withholding or granting wealth yields Withholder and Expander, while lowering or raising status yields Abaser and Exalter.
rows.anchor: إن حصل المنع والإعطاء في الأموال سمي قابضا باسطا وإن حصلا في الجاه والحشمة سمي خافضا رافعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God's possible creations across kinds and species are limitless, the names derived from creating specific things are limitless too.
rows.anchor: أقسام مقدورات الله تعالى بحسب الأنواع والأجناس غير متناهية فلا جرم يمكن أن يحصل لله تعالى أسماء غير متناهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some oppositions are contraries, such as exalting and humiliating or giving life and death; others are presence and absence, such as withholding versus extending or lowering versus raising.
rows.anchor: مقابل الشيء تارة يكون ضده وتارة يكون عدمه فقولنا : المعز المذل وقولنا المحيي المميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not honoring someone differs from actively humiliating them; the contrast between honor and abasement is a pair of opposites.
rows.anchor: فرق بين أن لا يعزه وبين أن يذله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ra'uf and Rahim are close, but Ra'uf leans toward conferring benefit whereas Rahim leans toward removing harm.
rows.anchor: الرؤوف الرحيم يقرب من هذا الباب إلا أن الرؤوف أميل إلى جانب إيصال النفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatih suggests creating the means of good; Wahib suggests conveying that good; Nafi suggests conveying benefit with the recipient's benefit in view.
rows.anchor: الفاتح يشعر بإحداث سبب الخير والواهب يشعر بإيصال ذلك الخير إليه والنافع يشعر بإيصال ذلك النفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic negations concern God's essence, attributes, or actions; negating every unlike essence or attribute yields an unlimited number of negative descriptions.
rows.anchor: ذلك السلب إما أن يكون عائدا إلى الذات أو إلى الصفات أو إلى الأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not a substance, body, in a place or space, or an indwelling subject or substrate; He is unlike other essences by His own specific essence.
rows.anchor: ليس جوهرا ولا جسما ولا في المكان ولا في الحيز ولا حالا ولا محلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's self-sufficiency means He needs nothing in His essence or real and negative attributes; the Lord is rich, possessed of mercy.
rows.anchor: كونه غنيا أنه لا يحتاج في ذاته ولا في صفاته الحقيقية ولا في صفاته السلبية إلى شيء غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God neither begets nor is begotten.
rows.anchor: لم يلد ولم يولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defects to be negated fall under the opposites of knowledge, power, self-sufficiency, and unity.
rows.anchor: كل صفة تكون من صفات النقائص فإنه يجب تنزيه الله تعالى عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God neither sleeps nor forgets nor is ignorant, and knowledge of one thing never distracts Him from another.
rows.anchor: رابعها أن علمه ببعض المعلومات لا يمنعه عن العلم بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's acts involve no fatigue, tools, material, or duration, and creating much or little takes no more time than an instant.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه منزه في أفعاله عن التعب والنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power does not end and He is not impoverished, contrary to the claim that God is poor and humans rich.
rows.anchor: رابعها نفي انتهاء القدرة وحصول الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion also includes negating partners, opposites, and peers under divine unity.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما يكون من باب أضداد الوحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God feeds but is not fed and protects others while none can overrule Him.
rows.anchor: ^ { وهو يطعم ولا يطعم } ^ [ الأنعام : 14 ] ^ { وهو يجير ولا يجار عليه } ^

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among negations of divine acts: God creates neither falsehood nor play nor purposelessness, but creates in truth.
rows.anchor: أحدها أنه لا يخلق الباطل قال تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not pleased with unbelief, does not will injustice, and does not love corruption.
rows.anchor: ورابعها أنه لا يرضى بالكفر قال تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He does not punish without prior wrongdoing; believers' gratitude and faith leave no need for punishment.
rows.anchor: وسابعها أنه لا يعاقب من غير سابقة جرم قال تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People's obedience benefits themselves and their wrongdoing harms themselves; God gains or loses nothing from them.
rows.anchor: أنه لا ينتفع بطاعات المطيعين ولا يتضرر بمعاصي المذنبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one may question God's actions and judgments; He does whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: وتاسعها : أنه ليس لأحد عليه اعتراض في أفعاله وأحكامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not break His word or promise and threat.
rows.anchor: وعاشرها : أنه لا يخلف وعده ووعيده قال تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since negations across God's essence, attributes, and actions are limitless, names arising from this class are limitless too.
rows.anchor: أقسام السلوب بحسب الذات وبحسب الصفات وبحسب الأفعال غير متناهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quddus describes God's essence as unlike deficient natures; Salam describes His freedom from deficient attributes.
rows.anchor: القدوس عبارة عن كون حقيقة ذاته مخالفة للماهيات التي هي نقائص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aziz means God has no equal; Ghaffar removes punishment from sinners; Halim does not hasten punishment and still grants mercy.
rows.anchor: العزيز وهو الذي لا يوجد له نظير وثالثها الغفار وهو الذي يسقط العقاب عن المذنبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahid means none shares God's unique essence or rivals Him in ordering the world and the affairs of the Throne.
rows.anchor: الواحد ومعناه أنه لا يشاركه أحد في حقيقته المخصوصة ولا يشاركه أحد في نظم العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghani means free of needs and necessities.
rows.anchor: الغني : ومعناه كونه منزها عن الحاجات والضرورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabur does not punish an offender despite power to do so; Halim does likewise while continuing to bestow blessings.
rows.anchor: الصبور هو الذي لا يعاقب المسيء مع القدرة عليه والحليم هو الذي يكون كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadir names God's power, illustrated by His ability to send punishment from above or below and to resurrect the dead and reconstruct their fingertips.
rows.anchor: الأول القادر قال تعالى : ﴿ قل هو القادر على أن يبعث عليكم عذابا من فوقكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadeer intensifies the description of God as powerful.
rows.anchor: هذا اللفظ يفيد المبالغة في وصفه بكونه قادرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqtadir is another name for power, used of God in the Quran.
rows.anchor: الثالث : المقتدر قال تعالى : ^ { وكان الله على كل شيء مقتدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God uses a plural form of the power name for Himself: We decreed, and how excellent are the decreers.
rows.anchor: الرابع : عبر عن ذاته بصيغة الجمع في هذه الصفة قال تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: King and owner imply power in a particular sense; malik occurs more often than malik meaning owner because kingship is a higher rank.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن لفظ الملك يفيد القدرة أيضا بشرط خاص ثم إن هذا اللفظ جاء في القرآن على وجوه مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other power-related forms include Owner of Sovereignty, Sovereign, and the kingdom that belongs to the Merciful on that day and of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: الثالث : مالك الملك قال تعالى : ﴿ قل اللهم مالك الملك ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quwwa is close in meaning to power; Quranic forms include the Strong and Possessor of Strength, the Firm.
rows.anchor: لفظ القوة يقرب من لفظ القدرة وقد جاء هذا اللفظ في القرآن على وجوه مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran affirms God's knowledge and uses forms including knower, all-knowing, most knowing, and past and future verbs of knowing.
rows.anchor: إثبات العلم لله تعالى قال تعالى : ^ { ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Quran says God teaches, do not call Him Teacher, because that name suggests deficiency.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يقال إن الله معلم مع كثرة هذه الألفاظ ؛ لأن لفظ المعلم مشعر بنوع نقيصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not call God al-Allama: although intensive, the form suggests that knowledge was gained through effort and strain.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز إطلاق لفظ العلامة على الله تعالى ؛ لأنها وإن أفادت المبالغة لكنها تفيد أن هذه المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabar and khibra nearly mean knowledge; some define knowledge as report, and the frequent divine name Khabir also indicates knowledge.
rows.anchor: لفظ الخبر والخبرة وهو كالمرادف للعلم حتى قال بعضهم في حد العلم : إنه الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahid means witness and knower when derived from seeing; if it means testimony, it belongs to speech instead.
rows.anchor: الشهيد في حق الله تعالى إذا فسرناه بكونه مشاهدا لها عالما بها أما إذا فسرناه بالشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hikma can mean knowledge or refraining from what is unsuitable and doing what is suitable.
rows.anchor: الحكمة وهذه اللفظة قد يراد بها العلم وقد يراد بها أيضا ترك ما لا ينبغي وفعل ما ينبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Latif can mean knowledge of subtle matters or conveying benefits to people through a hidden, wondrous means.
rows.anchor: اللطيف وقد يراد به العلم بالدقائق وقد يراد به إيصال المنافع إلى العباد بطريق خفية عجيبة
